 'Taking us for a ride': HC pulls up Kejriwal, AAP leaders over posts against Delhi judge with a warning 
 Trending PM Modi ASEAN Summit 2026 Sonia Gandhi Surya Kant Iran War Lateef Bhat IPL Retention PM Modi ASEAN Summit Cyclone Akvan Kulgam Terrorist Encounter PM Modi ASEAN Summit 2026 Sonia Gandhi Surya Kant Iran War Lateef Bhat IPL Retention PM Modi ASEAN Summit Cyclone Akvan Kulgam Terrorist Encounter PM Modi ASEAN Summit 2026 Sonia Gandhi Surya Kant Iran War Lateef Bhat IPL Retention PM Modi ASEAN Summit Cyclone Akvan Kulgam Terrorist Encounter 'Taking us for a ride': HC pulls up Kejriwal, AAP leaders over posts against Delhi judge with a warning 
 Edited by Vivek Dubey / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 17, 2026, 12:19 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print The court gave them three weeks to submit their responses NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Tuesday pulled up Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) supremo Arvind Kejriwal , Manish Sisodia, Saurabh Bharadwaj and other party leaders for failing to file their replies in a criminal contempt case over alleged social media posts targeting Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma. Granting the leaders a final opportunity, a division bench headed by Justice Navin Chawla gave them three weeks to submit their responses and warned that their right to file replies would be closed if they failed to comply. "We will not give you further time. You are taking us for a ride. We have report from the Registry that compliance has been done. You file your replies now otherwise we will close your right," the court orally observed, according to LiveLaw. Join conversation

 The suo motu contempt proceedings were initiated over allegations that a targeted social media campaign was launched to vilify Justice Sharma after she refused to recuse herself from hearing the Delhi excise policy case. Justice Sharma had earlier flagged the circulation of what she described as "extremely vilifying, extremely contemptuous, and defamatory material" against her and the court. While initiating contempt proceedings, she transferred the excise policy matter to another bench, citing judicial propriety and discipline. The contempt case is separate from the CBI's challenge to a trial court order discharging Kejriwal, Sisodia and 21 others in the excise policy case.
